records.name: 军事功绩奖章（Signum Laudis）
records.variant: 铜级镀金；弗朗茨·约瑟夫一世头像；材质按来源描述

evidence.source_excerpt: Instituted March 12 1890 by Emperor Franz Joseph I. (1890-1917). In bronze gilt, a medal with the obverse features a profile of Franz Joseph, the reverse presents the inscription SIGNVM LAVDIS surrounded by an oak and laurel wreath, the medal is surmounted by a large crown, measures 30.7mm (w) x 50.4mm (h), weighs 21.8 grams, worn on triangular ribbon, gilt wear on crown, small edge knocks, remains in near extremely fine condition. Contained in its case of issue, a red leatherette case with impressed coat of arms in silver on lid, interior presents a card lining on the lid and black velvet recessed medalbed, measures 61.9mm (w) x 107mm (h), hinge and catch functional, light wear to exterior, in very fine condition.

records.name: 功绩十字章
records.date: 1850年2月16日设立；来源称本件为1875–1914年版
records.variant: 金级、无冠；补配绶带；来源制造商描述冲突，待考

evidence.source_excerpt: (Goldenes Verdienstkreuz). Instituted 16 February 1850. (1875-1914 issue). In Gold, a beautiful decoration by Vincent Mayer & Sohne, comprising a Gold cross with red enamel arms, the obverse medallion featuring the raised initials FJ on a white enamelled disc, the reverse bears the date 1849, measures 29.6 mm (w) x 33.45 mm (h), weighs 6.92 grams, maker marked “A.KITTNER IN WEIN” on the suspension ring, worn on a replacement trifold ribbon, enamels intact, dent in the edge of the 3 o’clock arm, near extremely fine. Contained in the original case of issue, the black exterior with pebbled history with partial impression on the lid, the interior lid in silk, with green velvet medalbase, minor ripping and in the silk lid, measures 60 mm (w) x 100 mm (h) x 20 mm (d), functional hinge and clasp, very fine.

evidence.source_excerpt: (Goldenes Verdienstkreuz mit Krone). Instituted 16 February 1850. (1850-1918 issue). Military Division. Constructed of 18K Gold with multi-coloured enamels, consisting of a Cross with red enamelled arms, the obverse with a central white enamelled medallion bearing a central monogram of Franz Joseph I, circumscribed by an inscription of “VIRIBUS UNITIS” (“UNITED FORCES”), the reverse with a central white enamelled medallion bearing a gilt date of “1849”, on a gilded and enamelled crown suspension with loop connecting to a replacement tri-fold ribbon, the loop maker marked with Austrian Gold mark denoting manufacture between 1872-1922 and maker mark of Buc[hnuch?], measuring 35.7 mm (w) x 58.2 mm (h – inclusive of cross adorned crown suspension), weighs 16.39 grams (including ribbon), light wear to enamels, reverse 1849 slightly loose, the decoration remains in very fine condition.

evidence.source_excerpt: (Ehrenzeichen vom Roten Kreuz). Instituted August 14, 1914. Military Division. In silver, a red and white enamelled cross, obverse central medallion featuring a superimposed red cross on a white field, encircled by a red ring inscribed PATRIAE AC HUMANITATI, a green enamelled wreath lays across the arms, the reverse medallion features the dates 1864 1914, marked on the integral suspension with an Austrian silvermark denoting Vienna manufacture, worn on original trifold ribbon, measures 36.7 mm (w) x 48.4 mm (h), minor enamel wear and residue around the wreath, remains in very fine condition.

records.name: 1813—1814年军队十字章
records.variant: 炮铜十字章；来源称铜质镀金；具体实物年代待考

evidence.source_excerpt: (Armeekreuz). Instituted in 1814. In bronze gilt, designed as a paw cross and fabricated from bronze of captured French guns, measuring 27.8 mm (w) x 30.8 mm (h) inclusive of its integral loop, very light contact and surface wear, lightly soiled original triangular ribbon with hook and eye, near extremely fine. Footnote: The Army Cross 1813-1814 (AKA Cannon Cross) was instituted on May 13, 1814 by Emperor Franz I of Austria and could be awarded to all soldiers who took part in the wars of liberation against Napoleon.
